title: Capstone: LevelUp on a Linux server

cards.s: Capstone: LevelUp on a Linux server
cards.html: This chapter puts everything together. You deploy LevelUp's real FastAPI server on the lab VM so that it starts at boot, restarts on crash, keeps learners' progress in a protected data directory, logs to the journal, is sandboxed and memory-capped, and is health-checked every five minutes. Then you run the same app under Supervisor to compare, and finish with the final quiz.

RequirementHow
Starts at boot, after the networkWantedBy=multi-user.target, After=/Wants=network-online.target
Restarts on crash, without looping foreverRestart=on-failure, RestartSec=3, start limit 10 in 5 minutes
Runs unprivilegedSystem user levelup
Progress stored safely and persistentlyStateDirectory=levelup → /var/lib/levelup, passed as A1_DATA
Logs in the journalstdout, plus PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
Sandboxed and cappedThe chapter 7 block, MemoryMax=300M
Health-checkedA timer that calls /api/health

sudo useradd --system --home /opt/levelup --shell /usr/sbin/nologin levelup
sudo mkdir -p /opt/levelup && sudo chown $USER /opt/levelup
# copy LevelUp into /opt/levelup (from the Mac: multipass transfer, scp or git clone)
cd /opt/levelup/server_fastapi
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh && ~/.local/bin/uv sync --python /usr/bin/python3   # .venv on the system Python
sudo chown -R root:root /opt/levelup    # code is read-only to the service user

The server is started with python main.py <port> (it calls uvicorn.run itself) and reads its data folder from A1_DATA.

Why --python /usr/bin/python3: by default uv links the venv to a Python it downloaded into your home folder, and the ProtectHome=yes sandbox below hides home folders from the service, which would fail with 203/EXEC. Building the venv on the system Python avoids that trap.

/etc/systemd/system/levelup.service:

[Unit]
Description=LevelUp learning app (FastAPI)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=300
StartLimitBurst=10

[Service]
Type=exec
User=levelup
Group=levelup
WorkingDirectory=/opt/levelup/server_fastapi
StateDirectory=levelup
Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 A1_DATA=/var/lib/levelup
ExecStart=/opt/levelup/server_fastapi/.venv/bin/python main.py 8766
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
TimeoutStopSec=20

# sandbox
NoNewPrivileges=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
PrivateDevices=yes
ProtectKernelTunables=yes
ProtectKernelModules=yes
ProtectControlGroups=yes
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6
CapabilityBoundingSet=
SystemCallFilter=@system-service

# limits
MemoryMax=300M
TasksMax=100

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

StateDirectory= makes /var/lib/levelup writable even under ProtectSystem=strict, so no ReadWritePaths= line is needed. To keep existing progress, copy the Mac's progress/ files into /var/lib/levelup/ and chown -R levelup:levelup them.

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now levelup
curl -s localhost:8766/api/health
systemd-analyze security levelup

/etc/systemd/system/levelup-health.service:

[Unit]
Description=Restart LevelUp if /api/health stops answering

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'curl -fsS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8766/api/health >/dev/null || systemctl restart levelup'

/etc/systemd/system/levelup-health.timer:

[Timer]
OnBootSec=2min
OnUnitActiveSec=5min

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
Run sudo systemctl enable --now levelup-health.timer. The check runs as root, so it is allowed to restart the service. Its runs appear in journalctl -u levelup-health.

1. Crash: sudo kill -9 $(systemctl show -p MainPID --value levelup). A new PID about 3 seconds later.
  2. Reboot: sudo reboot, then systemctl is-active levelup and curl the health endpoint.
  3. Logs: journalctl -u levelup -b shows the kill, systemd's reaction and the restart.
  4. Hang: sudo kill -STOP $(systemctl show -p MainPID --value levelup) freezes the process without killing it. Within 5 minutes the health timer restarts it. A plain Restart= never would, because the process never exits.
  5. Data: use the app from your phone or browser (http://<vm-ip>:8766), then restart the service and check the progress is still there in /var/lib/levelup.

cards.s: Step 5: the same app under Supervisor
cards.html:
sudo systemctl disable --now levelup levelup-health.timer, then write /etc/supervisor/conf.d/levelup.conf:

[program:levelup]
command=/opt/levelup/server_fastapi/.venv/bin/python main.py 8766
directory=/opt/levelup/server_fastapi
user=levelup
environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1",A1_DATA="/var/lib/levelup",HOME="/opt/levelup"
autorestart=true
startsecs=5
stopwaitsecs=20
stopasgroup=true
killasgroup=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/log/supervisor/levelup.log

cards.s: Step 5: the same app under Supervisor
cards.html: Run sudo supervisorctl reread && sudo supervisorctl update, then repeat the crash test and tail -f. Write down three things systemd gave you that Supervisor didn't: the sandbox, the memory limit and the journal are the obvious ones. Then switch back to the systemd unit, the recommended set-up.

1. Which process is PID 1 on Ubuntu, and why does that matter for supervision?
  2. In what order does a supervisor send signals to stop a service, and which systemd and Supervisor settings control the wait?
  3. Wants=postgresql.service is set but After= isn't. What can go wrong?
  4. You ran systemctl enable app but it isn't running. Why?
  5. Which Type= should a foreground Uvicorn service use, and why that one over the default?
  6. Your unit has ExecStart=/opt/app/run.sh >> /var/log/app.log. What happens?
  7. Which Restart= value restarts after a crash but not after a clean exit?
  8. A service shows Result: start-limit-hit. How do you recover once the bug is fixed?
  9. Which command shows only errors for levelup since the last boot?

1. You enabled backup.service, but nothing runs at 03:30. What is wrong?
  2. What does ProtectSystem=strict do, and how does the app still write its data?
  3. A Supervisor program is in FATAL after a config change. Name the two commands you should have used, and where to look for the cause.
  4. Why shouldn't a Docker container run systemd or Supervisor inside it, and what should PID 1 be instead?
  5. The process is alive but every request hangs. Why doesn't Restart= help, and what does?
  6. On your Mac, which launchd folder and plist key keep the LevelUp server always running for your user?
🔒 Answers: try the questions first, then tap to show

1. systemd; it is the parent of every service, so it sees every exit and can restart and track them.
  2. SIGTERM, a grace period, then SIGKILL; TimeoutStopSec= and stopwaitsecs.
  3. Both start in parallel, so the app can start before the database is ready.
  4. enable only acts at boot; use start or enable --now.
  5. Type=exec: a broken ExecStart makes the start fail instead of looking successful.
  6. ExecStart isn't run by a shell, so >> and the path are passed as arguments; output goes to the journal anyway.
  7. on-failure.
  8. systemctl reset-failed levelup, then start it.
  9. journalctl -u levelup -b -p err.
  10. You must enable the timer (backup.timer), not the service.

1. It makes the whole filesystem read-only for the service; data goes in StateDirectory= or a ReadWritePaths= folder.
  2. supervisorctl reread and update; look at the program's log (tail x stderr) and supervisord.log.
  3. The container platform already supervises it, and you should run one foreground process per container; use a tiny init such as tini (--init) as PID 1.
  4. The process never exits, so nothing triggers a restart; add a health check (a timer with curl, a watchdog, httpok or a liveness probe).
  5. ~/Library/LaunchAgents/, with KeepAlive set to true (and RunAtLoad).

Score 12 or more out of 15 and you have mastered this branch.
